title: Username Search & Digital Footprint Checker | MyRecon
description: Search public usernames across supported platforms and check email breach exposure. Start a free Quick scan and verify profile matches at the source.
intro: MyRecon helps you review public username matches across supported sites. Enter a handle you own or are authorized to check, open any candidate at its source, and treat blocked or ambiguous checks as unknown.

sections.heading: Public username search
sections.body: A public username lookup starts from a handle and returns candidate pages only when a supported source can be checked. Coverage and availability vary by platform, so confirm the current profile instead of treating a missing result as proof that no account exists.

sections.heading: Review each result at its source
sections.body: Use the current MyRecon scanner for a self-audit or authorized review. This page explains the public-search workflow and its limits; it does not provide private-account discovery or guarantee a person's identity from a username.

sections.heading: Use public sources responsibly
sections.body: A responsible result review records the source URL, date, and visible evidence. Keep the task scoped, avoid bypassing platform controls, and leave blocked or uncertain checks unresolved.

cta.label: Search a public username with MyRecon

faq.question: What is a reverse username lookup and how does it work?
faq.answer: A reverse username lookup checks supported public profile pages for a handle. Results are leads, not proof of registration or ownership; review each match at its source. Read our reverse username lookup guide.

faq.question: What is a digital footprint check?
faq.answer: A digital footprint check audits your public online exposure by scanning registered usernames, checking whether your email was involved in data breaches, and identifying leaked credentials. See our digital footprint audit guide.

faq.question: Is MyRecon free to use?
faq.answer: MyRecon offers free guest Quick scans across 100 platforms, with no sign-up required. Only the first 2 result cards are visible; remaining cards are blurred. Standard scans across 500+ platforms require sign-in. Paid plans add Deep Search and Extended scans. See the current pricing page for features and limits.

faq.question: Does a username lookup confirm availability?
faq.answer: No. MyRecon checks public profile presence. A missing profile does not guarantee that a handle can be registered. Confirm username availability through the official platform signup or account settings flow.

faq.question: What is a social media username checker?
faq.answer: A social media username checker looks for public profiles using a handle across supported platforms. MyRecon helps you review those profile leads for your own digital footprint or authorized research. Verify important matches at the source.

faq.question: What can I check with MyRecon?
faq.answer: MyRecon includes public username, email and breach, password exposure, domain registration, DNS, and IP checks. Coverage and access can vary by tool, so use the live interface and current plan page to confirm what is available.

faq.question: Does a missing username result prove no account exists?
faq.answer: No. A site may block, rate-limit, rename, or restrict a profile, and some services may not be supported. Treat an unavailable or missing result as inconclusive unless the source provides a verifiable reason.

faq.question: Can MyRecon confirm that a profile belongs to a person?
faq.answer: No. A matching username is only a lead. Confirm important conclusions with independent public evidence and keep uncertain links unconfirmed. MyRecon does not access private accounts or restricted content.

product_claims: MyRecon supports a public username lookup workflow for checks available through its current platform catalogue; individual sites can be unavailable or change their behavior.
A result is a candidate for manual verification, not proof that a named person controls an account or that no account exists when no result appears.
